en: Washing towels and shirts morning to night,
hang 'em up, wash again. Nothing but this...
That chit of a girl Maud has it easy.
If I still had milk, I'd be a wet nurse too,
taking it a lot easier, I would.
And for far better wages than now
Hey, you! What are you peeping at?!
I'll yell for help! Shoo, off with you!
Make Claudia angry and you'll be sorry!
Oh, I hate it, hate it, hate it, hate it
What did I do to end up a laundress?
Huh? Oh, I wondered who it could be...
It's you. Here to see the master?
This is the servants' door. Go round south.
If it's the master you want, not this way.
Oh, what on earth did the master spill?
A stubborn stain like this won't come out.
And if it doesn't, it's my fault. I hate it.
Hm?
Back again? This is the servants' door.
Folks like you should use the south door.
Or are you here to help with the washing?
Oh, you again? Good of you to come.
Ha! 'Good of you to come,' listen to me.
What do you want with an old girl like me?
Good day, Claudia.
You look well. By the way...
<Why not change jobs?>
<Is the washing hard?>
Daft! I'd have done it long ago if I could.
I've no talents, so there's no helping it.
This is all the work a woman can get.
Ah, but that Maud gets my goat all the same.
She gets all that just for nursing a baby.
And yet she's so servile. Drives me mad!
Of course it is! What a thing to ask.
A man like you can't know what it's like.
Honestly! Women always suffer for men.
(It seems I've said something needless again.
Still, what a troublesome human...)
Well, never mind. Want to watch me wash?
Instead of loafing about,
go find yourself a hardworking wife too.
My, busy as ever today, eh?
Me, it's the same old thing: washing, washing.
It's grim, thinking this is my whole life
Yes, yes, who is it?
Home's the only place I get to rest, you know.
If it's nothing important, come back later.
Oh, I'm tired, so tired
You a hawker or something?
And I thought you just loafed about town.
I'm not buying anything. Go on, off with you.
Oh,
Come to hear gossip about the master?
Not a whiff of gossip about that one. Dull!
What, did you forget something?
! Fancy seeing you.
If you don't mind, keep me company a while.
Just working and sleeping is no way to live.
For you, the door's always open.
I'm just a lowly, poorly paid maid.
The name's Claudia.
(Some people really do have it hard.)
I was a beauty no man could leave alone.
There's something I'd like to ask you.
I seem to have lost my way,
so please, my lady, um
Spare me the flattery.
I'm only a laundress.
I'll do this hard work till the day I die.
Oh, I hate it, I hate it...
Ah, she's gone.
Oh well, I'll just have to walk and find it
No use asking me the way.
Good evening. I'm well, thank you.
And how is your work going?
Oh, I-I'm in a bit of a hurry, so
I'm sorry. I'll call again another time.
Well, I never! Listen to your elders, boy
